**Illustrative interview answer—not a claim about your experience:** “I built a support-ticket routing system. We defined success as correctly resolved tickets per agent-hour, with escalation and latency guardrails. A keyword heuristic handled obvious cases; logistic regression on text features was the first learned baseline. Its error analysis showed context-dependent routing and rare-team confusion, so we tested a pretrained encoder rather than assuming a larger model was necessary.” [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml)

“I used time-separated evaluation, checked duplicate tickets and label timing, compared per-team precision/recall, and measured serving cost. A shadow deployment exposed feature-parity bugs before a randomized rollout. I would report the actual measured lift and confidence interval, plus a failed approach and my individual contribution.” Replace the scenario and results with your own verified work; never invent a metric to make the story impressive.
